definitions.explanation: A physically deep spot, such as a deep part of a river, pool, or body of water.
Abstract depth or richness in quality, such as depth of flavor, color, meaning, or character.

examples.japanese: {川|かわ}の{深|ふか}みに{足|あし}を{取|と}られた。
examples.english: I lost my footing in a deep part of the river.

examples.japanese: {深|ふか}みにはまらないように{気|き}をつけて。
examples.english: Be careful not to get in over your head.
examples.notes: Can refer literally to deep water or figuratively to getting too deeply involved.

examples.japanese: このプールは{奥|おく}に{行|い}くほど{深|ふか}みが{増|ま}す。
examples.english: This pool gets deeper the further back you go.

examples.japanese: {年齢|ねんれい}とともに{味|あじ}わいに{深|ふか}みが{出|で}た。
examples.english: The flavor gained depth with age.

examples.japanese: この{絵|え}には{色|いろ}の{深|ふか}みがある。
examples.english: This painting has depth of color.

examples.japanese: {経験|けいけん}を{積|つ}むことで{人間|にんげん}としての{深|ふか}みが{増|ま}す。
examples.english: By accumulating experience, one gains depth as a person.

notes:
USAGE:
Formed from {深|ふか}い (deep) + the suffix ～み (which forms nouns indicating degree or quality). The figurative sense (sense 2) is particularly common, used to describe richness or profundity in abstract qualities.

The expression {深|ふか}みにはまる means both "to step into deep water" literally and "to get in too deep" figuratively.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {深|ふか}みが{増|ま}す: to gain depth
- {深|ふか}みがある: to have depth
- {深|ふか}みにはまる: to get in too deep
- {味|あじ}に{深|ふか}みがある: to have depth of flavor
